chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan, from Hammad ibn 'Isa, from Rib'i, from Muhammad ibn Muslim, from Abu Ja'far عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him: May a man perform salat (prayer) while he is veiled over the mouth? He said: As for on the ground, no; but as for on a riding animal, there is no harm.

key_terms.الرَّجُلُ: the man asking about the ruling
key_terms.عَلَى الْأَرْضِ: while on the ground, meaning normal standing prayer
key_terms.فَلَا بَأْسَ: there is no harm; it is permitted
key_terms.مُتَلَثِّمٌ: covering the mouth or lower face with a veil

ai.seo_question: Can a man perform salat (prayer) while covering his mouth with a veil?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on performing salat (prayer) while covering the mouth with a litham. It indicates that doing so on the ground is not permitted, while doing so during prayer on a riding animal is allowed, showing a distinction in rulings based on circumstance.
